citations.title: Solar Open 2: Korea's Sovereign Foundation Model, Built for Agentic Use
excerpts: Today we're releasing Solar Open 2, our open-weight foundation model optimized for agentic use.

Solar Open 2 is designed and trained to serve as the base model for agents in real work environments. It's trained on a wide range of agent scenarios, including tool calling, coding, and office work, and delivers performance that competes with leading global models across agent, Korean, knowledge, and coding benchmarks.

The model adopts an MoE architecture that activates only 15B of its 250B total parameters per token, improving capability and inference efficiency at the same time. With quantization, it runs on two NVIDIA H200 GPUs, which makes it practical for enterprises to deploy and operate on their own infrastructure. Built for agent tasks that run across many steps, it supports a context window of up to 1M tokens and comes with official support for Korean, English, and Japanese.

The model weights are released on Hugging Face under a commercially usable license. Alongside them, we publish the Solar Open 2 Technical Report, covering the full architecture, training methodology, key experiments, and evaluation conditions.

basis.reasoning: The blog index lists the on-device LLM post. That post describes quantization and engine optimization and credits four authors; the Solar Open 2 post describes the model architecture and training methodology. Together these establish multiple substantive technical posts rather than only marketing or release notes.

citations.title: Upstage eyes $3.3B valuation as AI startup races toward year-end IPO - The Herald Business
excerpts: Upstage eyes $3.3B valuation as AI startup races toward year-end IPO by Cha Min-ju Published : June 15, 2026 - 16:54:15

Upstage reshuffled its C-suite earlier this year, most notably bringing in Jin Yun-jeong, a capital markets specialist from early investor SBVA, as CFO. Existing executive Kwon Sun-il, formerly executive vice president for business, was elevated to chief strategy officer, while Ryu Han-na, who oversaw management support, became chief operating officer. The moves completed a six-member C-suite combining the three founding members — CEO Kim Sung-hoon, Chief Technology Officer Lee Hwal-seok and Chief Product Officer Park Eun-jeong — with dedicated finance, strategy and operations leadership.
